title: Sync upload HTTP batches and complete delivery results v1
description: Root describes the existing batch success shape, including per-entry validation rejection. The separate checked-envelope anchor describes the stricter shared client profile; Gateway does not invoke that complete parser.
$comment: Source-only. Register sync-consumer.json and sync-changes.json alongside this resource. Runtime checks ordinary finite JSON, Unicode scalars/UTF-16 limits, original identity, normalized fingerprints and cross-request relationships. Legacy raw HTTP input and SDK snapshot acceptance differ. No schema authenticates a sender or proves source application.

idempotencyKey.$comment: validateIdempotencyKey uses UTF-16 length and rejects whitespace, but does not itself reject every control or lone surrogate. Preserve the original value. HTTP headers/database constraints may be narrower.

source_refs.description: Omitted or null normalizes to []; preserve original presence and order when saving a request.

sensitivity.description: Omitted or null normalizes to internal. This is claimed event sensitivity, not permission to read restricted data.

SyncUploadEvent.$comment: Matches parseSyncUploadEvent's structural profile, not per-entry business acceptance. No event-type whitelist. Entire raw event, including extra keys/values, rejects NUL/lone surrogates and nonfinite numbers. Parsing retains only event_id/event_type/payload/source_refs/sensitivity/client_cursor for the event fingerprint; SDK snapshot and original-receipt echo retain raw extras. FieldChangeProposed business validation is separate. Explicit outer identity extras must equal verified context at upload, or original identity at receipt query.

FieldChangePayload.description: Business shape checked only for event_type=FieldChangeProposed after replay and client sequence checks. Value is required but may be null/any JSON; no field-specific value model or source update is implied. Extra payload fields remain part of the event fingerprint/content.

events.description: Legacy handler accepts raw entries and reports invalid entries individually, even nonobjects or invalid IDs. Prefer SyncUploadClientBatch for prepared valid inputs.

idempotency_key.description: Legacy fallback used only without Idempotency-Key header. Selected key must satisfy idempotencyKey; a present header wins without comparing this body value.

expected_version.description: Legacy field participates in the batch fingerprint; when a version header exists this value must match it. It does not provide CAS for the source entity.

SyncUploadHttpBody.$comment: Raw body is parsed as a JSON object within 1 MiB before authentication. Unknown outer fields are not rejected and affect batch fingerprint, except idempotency_key is removed. Duplicate event IDs are not globally rejected by Gateway. Query parameters are not batch inputs.

SyncUploadClientBatch.$comment: SDK/Bridge shared snapshot profile: {events} <=1 MiB, ordinary finite JSON, depth64/nodes100000, event_id unique, raw optional-field presence/extras retained. FieldChangeProposed business validity is still checked by server. Original batch key and optional expected_identity are transport/options metadata, not this body.

RejectedUpload.description: Only VERSION_CONFLICT has a persisted server event/conflict. Other rejections have no delivery fields. Invalid raw IDs become the empty string in legacy validation rejection. Rejection traces can be historical after batch replay.

SyncUploadEnvelope.$comment: Intended complete legacy HTTP output. Combined item count equals batch size, outer cursor=next_cursor and source ID=project. Gateway does not run the shared 256 KiB response validator or fully revalidate stored batch receipts/high-water before replay; corrupt/unsafe results are not made valid by this schema. Repeated raw event IDs can produce repeated delivery entries. No request-key/identity/fingerprint echo, replay flag, revision or ETag.

SyncUploadCheckedEnvelope.$comment: Shared SDK/Bridge parser additionally enforces 256 KiB/finite JSON/depth64/nodes100000, exact request trace/scope, each original event exactly once, unique server IDs/positions/conflict IDs, delivery positions<=next_cursor, VERSION_CONFLICT only for FieldChangeProposed, CURSOR_GAP only for supplied differing client_cursor and exact source. JSON Schema alone cannot enforce these original-request relationships. Checked output does not prove source application or bind the original batch key.
